goal.text: Turn one meeting's notes into a clean list of action items, so nobody has to re-read the notes to know who does what by when.

agent_checkable.metric: Actions backed by a quoted sentence from the notes
agent_checkable.check: The critic checks every row's source against the notes (Q01).

agent_checkable.metric: Commitments in the notes that appear in the list
agent_checkable.check: Evaluation cases with a reference list (field recall).

outcome.metric: Lists handed to the volunteers without reopening the notes

users_and_stakeholders.interest: Knows who does what by when after each meeting.
Approves each list before it is shared.

steps: Someone re-reads the notes the next day.
They type an action list by hand.
problems: Two people sometimes do the same job.

in: One meeting's notes as plain text in, one action-item list out.
out: More than one meeting at a time

samples.description: Repair café committee notes, a fair sample.

glossary.meaning: Someone says they will do something; 'let's discuss it later' is not one.

acceptance_tests.words: I will know it worked when I can hand the list to the volunteers without opening the notes again.
cites: [A:A08 "I will know it worked when I can hand the list to the volunteers without opening the notes again."]

context_inventory.evidence_for: What real-length input looks like; source of the sample actions.

cites: [A:A12 "All notes are made up for testing."]

ranks.what: The meeting notes in the context pack
ranks.use_for: Every action, owner and due date
Not used: nothing from the web

confidence.high: The action is quoted word for word from the notes.
confidence.medium: Not used: every action needs a quote.
confidence.low: Not used: an action without a quote is left out.

conflicts: If two sentences in the notes disagree, list both and say so; never pick one silently.

output.format: Markdown table, rendered by a script from the validated list

fields.name: owner
fields.description: An attendee's name from the notes, or 'unassigned'.

fields.name: source
fields.description: The sentence the action came from, quoted.

rules.statement: Every action is backed by a quoted sentence from the notes; nothing invented.
cites: [A:A07 "Every action needs a quoted sentence from the notes; that is major."]

rules.statement: Owner and due date come only from the notes; otherwise 'unassigned' or 'not stated'.
Nothing missed and no duplicates: every commitment appears exactly once.
Every action starts with a verb.

definitions: A commitment is when someone says they will do something; 'let's discuss it later' is not a commitment.

good.text: A1 | Send the revised budget to the team | Priya | Friday 31 Oct | Priya will send the revised budget by Friday.
A2 | Collect the spare-parts box | unassigned | not stated | Someone needs to collect the spare-parts box.

bad.text: A3 | Book the venue | Tom | next week | (no source)
bad.why: The owner and date are guessed and nothing is quoted.

bad.text: A4 | the toaster sign-up sheet | Mia | not stated | Mia will print the toaster sign-up sheet.
bad.why: It does not start with a verb.

risk.notes: Nothing is written anywhere; a wrong list is fixed by hand.

gates.decision: Approve or reject each reviewed list before it is shared.
cites: [A:A11 "I want to approve every list before it goes out."]

open_questions.question: Will the list also be needed as a spreadsheet later?

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The writer and the critic meet the evaluation thresholds on synthetic notes like the sample.
Every list passes the approver's gate before it is shared.
